candidates.name: Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma
support_spans: multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion on the left side
Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
Immunoreactive for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, Wilms tumor protein 1
Neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, confirming mesothelial origin
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with pleural thickenings and effusion, along with the pathological findings of epithelioid solid formations and immunoreactivity for mesothelial markers, support this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Metastatic Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma
support_spans: Nodular growth observed on the mid third of the tongue
Neoplastic subepithelial proliferation, consisting of epithelioid cells in the tongue
Neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, confirming mesothelial origin
candidates.why: The appearance of a nodular growth on the tongue with pathological findings consistent with mesothelioma suggests metastasis.

candidates.name: Metastatic Malignant Mesothelioma to the Tongue
support_spans: Nodular growth observed on the mid third of the tongue.
Neoplastic subepithelial proliferation, consisting of epithelioid cells in the tongue
candidates.why: The appearance of a nodular growth on the tongue with histological findings consistent with mesothelioma suggests metastasis to this site.

candidates.name: Sarcomatoid Mesothelioma
support_spans: homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene by fluorescent in-situ hybridization
candidates.why: The genetic finding of CDKN2A deletion is more commonly associated with sarcomatoid mesothelioma, a subtype of malignant mesothelioma.
candidates.protected_reason: This subtype is less common than epithelioid mesothelioma and may be underdiagnosed.
